info.title: API.SH: crates.io
info.description: The crates.io API from API.SH: public crates.io data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
Searches crates.io, the Rust package registry. Filter by category, keyword, all of several keywords, publisher (user or team) or first letter, and sort by relevance, all-time downloads, recent downloads, recent updates, newest or name. Each crate comes with description, versions, all-time and 90-day downloads, links and dates. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`; null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/crates-io-search

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search words (optional when a filter is given).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order (default relevance with q, else downloads).

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Category slug, e.g. encoding or web-programming::http-client (see /crates-io/v1/categories).

parameters.name: keyword
parameters.description: One keyword, e.g. cli.

parameters.name: all_keywords
parameters.description: Space-separated keywords that must all be present.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Only crates this publisher owns: a crates.io login (dtolnay) or a team (github:org:team).

parameters.name: letter
parameters.description: Only crates starting with this letter.

parameters.name: include_yanked
parameters.description: true to include fully yanked crates.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Results per page, 1-100 (default 20).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` from the previous page; null on the last page.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
